description:
Scope: coverage planning only for lib/zaq/channels/jido_chat_bridge/incoming/telegram.ex:27. Existing cover/excoveralls.json reports line 27 as the only zero-hit line in this module; report is observational, not fresh validation. Do not change production code.

Exclusive test path: test/zaq/channels/incoming_normalization_test.exs (extend its existing async: true ExUnitProperties module). No Telegram webhook test, integration route, support file, or additional test file is needed.

Test-first steps:
1. Reuse the existing Telegram meta/raw fixtures in the test at lines 25-38: meta %{chat_type: :private, is_dm: true, external_room_id: "-100123"}; raw %{"chat" => %{"id" => -100_123, "type" => "private"}, "date" => 1_700_000_000}. Add a focused test or table-driven assertions for raw = nil and raw = an unexpected non-map (e.g. [] or "invalid"), with otherwise valid meta. For each, assert exactly {:error, :unverified_communication_facts} = Telegram.normalize(meta, raw, nil). These values fail the `when is_map(raw)` guard, exercising the otherwise-uncovered catch-all at line 27 rather than the with/else at line 23.
2. Also pass missing/incomplete metadata (nil and/or a map lacking :is_dm) with valid raw; assert the identical error. This exercises the unmatched first argument of line 27, independently of the raw guard. A valid-input control already exists at lines 25-34; the conflicting type assertion at lines 36-37 already exercises the with/else rejection. Keep at least one valid control alongside new assertions so future accidental over-rejection fails.
3. Assert only the public return contract, not private helper calls, exception text, or implementation details. No DB, HTTP, processes, global configuration, Mox, fake adapters, sleeps or timing polling. Reuse in-file literals; no helper abstraction or fixture factory necessary. Remain async: true; if a future change adds global-state mutation, split that scenario to async: false with on_exit restoration, not here.

Property assessment: The existing room-mismatch property at lines 70-80 covers a broad invariant. The uncovered guard is a finite malformed-shape partition; table-driven examples are sufficient, no new property or generator. If testing broader arbitrary terms later, only include shapes whose contract is fail-closed and do not duplicate the existing property.

Validation ownership: implementer runs ONLY `mix test test/zaq/channels/incoming_normalization_test.exs` after writing tests; do not run full suite, coveralls, mix q, or test execution during this planning task. Parent owns mix q and final targeted --cover verification. Confirm the final targeted coverage reports line 27 hit, and recheck report path/source version; a stale report or instrumentation mismatch is a blocker to claiming success. No known unreachable lines: both raw guard failure and metadata mismatch reach line 27 through normalize/3 directly. If the line still misses despite the direct tests, report instrumentation/report mismatch to parent rather than adding test-only production hooks. E2E approval gate not applicable: existing pure normalization unit coverage, not a new feature/UI.
